channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: Asian Shares Slide Sharply as Doubts Over the AI Boom Return
item.description: Shares across Asia fell sharply on Wednesday as renewed doubts about the artificial intelligence boom hammered chipmakers, wiping out the relief rally that followed Jensen Huang's return to the top of Nvidia.

item.title: US Set to Unveil New Tariffs on 16 Trading Partners After Excess-Capacity Probe
item.description: The United States is poised to unveil new tariffs on 16 major trading partners, including China and the European Union, after an investigation into excess industrial capacity, with the announcement expected as soon as Tuesday.

item.title: Ábrego García Leaves US for Spain, Ending Two-Year Deportation Battle
item.description: Kilmar Ábrego García, a 31-year-old Salvadoran sheet-metal worker from Maryland, is leaving the United States for Spain on Tuesday, closing a legal fight that lasted nearly two years and at one point reached the country's highest court.

item.title: CIA and National Intelligence Office Suffer Apparent Cyberattack on Unclassified System
item.description: The CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence have suffered an apparent cyberattack affecting unclassified information, in the latest breach to hit the United States government.

item.title: Eisenkot Clinches First Coalition Deal as Lieberman Joins Bid to Form Government
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot has secured the first coalition agreement in his bid to form Israel's next government, with Avigdor Lieberman's party agreeing to join him after the two men met on Tuesday.

item.title: AI Boom Breathes New Life Into San Francisco, but Fears of a Crash Are Growing
item.description: San Francisco is enjoying an artificial intelligence boom that is breathing new life into a city hollowed out by the pandemic, but some of the people building the technology now fear the sector is heading for a fall.

item.title: Five Killed as Turkish Military Helicopter Crashes During Training Flight
item.description: Five Turkish Air Force crew members were killed on Tuesday evening when their helicopter crashed during a training flight in western Turkiye, the defence ministry said.

item.title: DR Congo Rebels Call Off Advance on Bunia and Pull Back After Days of Fighting
item.description: A rebel group in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has halted its advance on the city of Bunia and begun pulling back from territory it seized in recent days, after heavy fighting with government forces displaced thousands of civilians.

item.title: Huawei Found Guilty of Stealing Trade Secrets and Bank Fraud in US Trial
item.description: A federal jury in Brooklyn has convicted Chinese telecoms giant Huawei of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, after a trial lasting almost three months.

item.title: Putin Says Retaliation Is Inevitable as Ukraine Keeps Hitting Russian Oil Refineries
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has said retaliation is inevitable after Ukraine kept striking Russian oil refineries, despite a direct request from US President Donald Trump to stop.

item.title: About 175 Migrants Missing After Boat From Senegal Vanishes En Route to Europe
item.description: Around 175 people are unaccounted for after a migrant boat that sailed from Dakar about two weeks ago fell silent on its way to Europe, local officials and a rights group said.

item.title: Senior Erdogan Ally Quits Ruling Party Post as Fund Probe Reaches His Son
item.description: Hayati Yazici, a founder of Turkey's ruling AK Party and a former minister, has resigned from the party leadership after a criminal probe into alleged stock-market manipulation widened to include his son.

item.title: Trump Officials Split Over Targeting Iran's Leaders to End the War
item.description: Officials in President Donald Trump's administration are debating whether American forces should strike at senior Iranian leaders in a bid to remove hardliners and end the nine-month war, according to a report.

item.title: Xiamen Airlines Signs $7.4 Billion Deal for 50 Boeing 737-8 Jets
item.description: Xiamen Airlines has agreed to buy 50 Boeing 737-8 jets in a deal worth about $7.4 billion at list prices, the planemaker's first big order from a Chinese carrier in nearly ten years.

item.title: Mosque Loudspeaker Seizures in Israel Draw 'Religious War' Accusation Against Ben-Gvir
item.description: Israel's national security minister has been accused of trying to start a religious war after police seized loudspeakers from two mosques in the south of the country.

item.title: Leaked Russian Records Put War Dead at 720,000, Investigation Finds
item.description: The death toll among Russian soldiers since the invasion of Ukraine began in 2022 is close to three quarters of a million, according to a joint investigation by two independent Russian news outlets working from leaked government death records.

item.title: Israel Says Iran Is Developing Chemical Weapons and Plotting to Kill Trump
item.description: Israel's defence minister said on Tuesday that Iran has begun developing chemical weapons since the war in February, and claimed Tehran has ordered the killing of the US president and members of his family.

item.title: Ten Hostages Freed in Cartagena Supermarket Standoff, Reports Say All Are Out
item.description: Ten hostages have been freed from a supermarket in Cartagena where gunmen seized about 30 people after a botched robbery, police said, and local media reported that all of the hostages were eventually released.

item.title: Landmine Toll Reaches Five-Year High as Myanmar and Syria Bear the Brunt
item.description: More people were killed or wounded by landmines and leftover explosives in 2025 than in any year since 2020, a global monitoring report said on Tuesday, with Myanmar and Syria accounting for nearly half of all victims.

item.title: Russian Governor Detained in Rare Corruption Case Against Regional Leader
item.description: Russia has detained the governor of its northern Murmansk region on suspicion of embezzlement, the Interior Ministry said on Monday, in the first criminal case against a regional leader in five years.

item.title: US Army to Detonate Five Tons of Unstable Explosives in Iowa on Wednesday
item.description: The US Army will carry out a controlled detonation of nearly five tons of unstable explosive material at an ammunition plant in Iowa on Wednesday morning, after a federal appeals court cleared the way for the operation on Monday evening.

item.title: US Sanctions on Hezbollah-Linked Groups May Have Limited Impact, Analysts Say
item.description: New American sanctions on organisations linked to Hezbollah are unlikely to weaken the group much beyond the political message they send, analysts have said, six days after Washington announced the measures.

item.title: Seven Killed as Suspected Gas Blast Flattens Hanoi Hot Pot Eatery
item.description: An explosion at a hot pot restaurant in Vietnam's capital, Hanoi, killed seven people and injured nine on Tuesday morning, in a blast officials suspect was caused by leaking cooking gas.

item.title: Riyadh's Tallest Tower Struck Again as 11 Injured in Financial District Attack
item.description: A projectile hit a tower in Riyadh's financial district on Tuesday, injuring 11 people in the second strike on the area in under a week, Saudi authorities said.

item.title: China Places Shanghai Party Chief Chen Jining Under Corruption Investigation
item.description: China has placed Chen Jining, the Communist Party chief of Shanghai and a member of its ruling Politburo, under investigation for suspected corruption, in the most senior fall yet of the party's widening anti-graft campaign.

item.title: Senegal Reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations Champions After Winning Court Appeal
item.description: Senegal have been reinstated as champions of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after sport's highest court backed their challenge to the decision that took the trophy away.

item.title: Two Arrested After Break-In at William and Kate's Country Home in Norfolk
item.description: Police in eastern England said on Tuesday that two men had been arrested following a reported break-in at the country residence of Prince William and Princess Catherine.

item.title: Britain Freezes Houthi Assets and Sanctions Four Senior Officials
item.description: Britain has imposed sanctions on Yemen's Houthi movement and four of its senior officials, freezing the group's assets and accusing the officials of torture, rape and other serious abuses of detainees.

item.title: Iraq Orders Federal Takeover of Kurdish Oilfields and Border Crossings
item.description: Iraq's prime minister has ordered the federal government to take over oilfields and border crossings in the country's Kurdistan region, a sweeping move the Kurdistan regional government immediately rejected.

item.title: Malaysia to Send More Than 6,500 Myanmar Nationals Back to Myanmar
item.description: Malaysia will send more than 6,500 Myanmar nationals back to Myanmar in December, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim told parliament on Tuesday, five days after the World Court ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority.
